Fix PR review setup, worker lifecycle, and bundle handling.

## Description

This PR changes four files:

- `.github/skills/review-pull-request/SKILL.md`: activate the trusted guidance checkout environment in the same shell as native preparation. If the pinned SDK is missing, provision it through the repository's SDK-only `eng/common/dotnet.ps1` or `eng/common/dotnet.sh` entrypoint, then reactivate. Setup remains exclusive to a native local coordinator without a supplied bundle. Do not switch, pull, stash, or clean the guidance checkout, substitute an SDK, or edit `global.json`; return `BLOCKED` when supported setup fails. Dispatch prescribed guide workers in background mode, wait for completion notification, and collect their actual reports with `read_agent(wait: true)`, including after same-worker clarification. For hosted bundle reads, require authorized native readers/searches and size-aware paging; distinguish shell denial from file denial and carry these read rules into hosted worker briefs.
- `.github/skills/review-pull-request/scripts/Directory.Build.props`: set `TargetFramework` to `$(BundledNETCoreAppTargetFramework)` only when `$(FileBasedProgram)` is `true`. The trusted file-based helper uses the selected SDK's bundled framework; explicit project targeting is untouched.
- `.github/skills/review-pull-request/scripts/prepare-review.cs`: make the emitted execution exclusion agree with the skill's existing optional native-coordinator repro rules, and require the same first-exclusion scope/reason when reusing a bundle.
- `.github/skills/review-pull-request/tests/PrepareReviewTests.cs`: assert the emitted contract for real local/remote preparation and reject changed scope, changed reason, or the legacy blanket exclusion during reuse.

### Why the helper correction is necessary

The first fresh, uncoached native review at instruction commit `b3c6b4f94dbba01975dbd0f1fa616432c9e33e9f` started without a local SDK. It loaded the exact committed skill, installed the pinned SDK `12.0.100-alpha.1.26521.103` through the supported script, and reactivated without caller help. It then stopped **BLOCKED** before producing a manifest: the generated helper targeted `net11.0` and required `Microsoft.NETCore.App 11.0.0-preview.7.26381.103`, while the SDK installed runtime `12.0.0-alpha.1.26521.103`. No review workers or final synthesis ran. This original result remains blocked; it is not relabeled by later validation.

The cause was traced to the installed SDK's exact source/binary, not assumed cache contamination: [`Product.TargetFrameworkVersion` is hardcoded to `"11.0"`](https://github.com/dotnet/dotnet/blob/ee344f85ef890dd92974e9b93d75906f1f8c39f3/src/sdk/src/Cli/Microsoft.DotNet.Cli.CoreUtils/Product.cs#L13), and its file-app virtual project uses that default. SDK bundled-version metadata maps `net11.0` to the missing preview runtime. The virtual project sets `FileBasedProgram` before importing SDK props; bundled framework properties are available when the helper-local `Directory.Build.props` is imported.

The inspected default branch `ceb0eec49d8d2c77f4f7c26b85ddb6e96940dfed` carries the same helper/setup inputs; its SDK12 pin was introduced by `c7bd3dd4616af5efce3b59634c4d946399b4095a`. This was not introduced by the setup paragraph. The SDK-only entrypoints call `InitializeDotNetCli` with installation enabled. Full restore separately processes configured runtimes, but those currently resolve to runtime12, not the missing runtime11; replacing SDK-only setup with full restore does not correct this mismatch.

The one conditional property avoids an undeclared older-runtime prerequisite without hardcoding a TFM, adding runtime11, changing roll-forward, substituting SDKs, or importing product build infrastructure. Frozen-bundle handling, review criteria, worker count/type/model, same-worker/no-relaunch rules, evidence/status gates, publication restrictions, and existing execution boundaries are unchanged. No product code, SDK pins, dependency manifests, NuGet configuration, or shared installations change.

### Why the lifecycle clarification is necessary

A second fresh uncoached review at helper-corrected commit `c1a8ec25a222ef90f0aefa9ba7d6e1e30872dfb9` recovered the naturally missing SDK and produced its own real manifest. The prescribed `general-purpose` / `gpt-5.6-sol` worker returned, but it had been dispatched synchronously. When the coordinator requested candidate clarification from that same worker, `write_agent` rejected it with `Agent is not running in background mode` (`not_background`). The skill required an incomplete result when the worker could not receive the clarification, so the final result was **INCOMPLETE**. That trial is retained unchanged; successful setup alone does not satisfy full-review completion.

The skill required same-worker clarification without specifying the runtime mode that permits it. The short lifecycle instruction makes dispatch and result collection explicit; it does not relax candidate evidence requirements or replace/relaunch workers.

### Why the manifest exclusion correction is necessary

The skill already permits a native local coordinator without a supplied bundle to optionally run a minimal test or repro in a temporary detached worktree at `manifest.target.head`. The helper instead emitted a blanket exclusion of running PR code, tests, CI, browser workflows, or implementation samples, described as an entirely source-only review. The inspected default branch has the same contradiction. Removing that contradiction is justified independently of whether it influenced an earlier unverified review candidate; no causal attribution or improved review accuracy is claimed.

The first exclusion now explicitly preserves source-only workers, hosted runs, and supplied-bundle runs. Only the existing native-local/no-supplied-bundle exception is described: a minimal detached-head test or repro, never execution in the developer checkout or bundle, exact command/result recording, and cleanup. Unavailable optional execution remains valid source-only review, not `INCOMPLETE`. No execution functionality, role detection, mandatory test requirement, or skill/evidence/publication rule changes are added by this follow-up.

Generation and reuse validation share the exact first-exclusion scope/reason constants. Reuse still requires two exclusions and the existing second policy snapshot; it additionally rejects a modified or legacy first exclusion rather than accepting stale contradictory instructions.

### Validation

All `dotnet` commands below followed `. .\activate.ps1` in the same PowerShell process. `$evidence` denotes the retained artifact root used by the recorded commands:

```powershell
$evidence = Join-Path $env:USERPROFILE '.copilot\session-state\d0e1c19d-93c0-4db5-8721-b70c959d52a8\files'
```

1. **Fresh-output bootstrap red/green**, same frozen #70024 head `d3068c868d2fafeb5f3a37f94c4d8637ce063ed0`, same pinned SDK12. The original helper at clean `b3c6b4f...` failed with exit `-2147450730`, requiring runtime11; its new generated assets/runtimeconfig confirmed `net11.0`. The corrected helper succeeded with exit `0`, generated `net12.0`/runtime12 metadata, and returned a real `ready: true`, version-2 manifest at the requested head. Baseline and candidate used different previously absent artifact/output directories and `--no-cache`:

   ```powershell
   dotnet run --no-cache --artifacts-path "$evidence\helper-baseline-artifacts" .\.github\skills\review-pull-request\scripts\prepare-review.cs -- --pr 70024 --head d3068c868d2fafeb5f3a37f94c4d8637ce063ed0 --output "$evidence\helper-baseline-bundle"
   dotnet run --no-cache --artifacts-path "$evidence\helper-candidate-artifacts" .\.github\skills\review-pull-request\scripts\prepare-review.cs -- --pr 70024 --head d3068c868d2fafeb5f3a37f94c4d8637ce063ed0 --output "$evidence\helper-candidate-bundle"
   ```

2. **Explicit test-project targeting control passed.** On both baseline and candidate, actual MSBuild evaluation returned `TargetFramework=net11.0`, empty `FileBasedProgram`, and `BundledNETCoreAppTargetFramework=net12.0`. Restored test assets also retained `net11.0`:

   ```powershell
   dotnet msbuild .\.github\skills\review-pull-request\scripts\PrepareReview.Tests.csproj '-getProperty:TargetFramework,FileBasedProgram,BundledNETCoreAppTargetFramework'
   ```

3. **Default helper-test configuration remains blocked.** During the SDK-helper correction, the following command failed identically on untouched baseline and candidate with `MSB3030`: generated `obj\PrepareReview.Tests\debug\apphost.exe` was missing. Both attempts exited `1` before test assertions or application launch. The baseline used `helper-baseline-tests-artifacts` instead of `helper-tests-artifacts`. The explicit project remains on runtime11; no older runtime was installed and no unrelated test/configuration fix was added. The execution-exclusion follow-up reconfirmed this default-command failure with the separate `exclusion-default-tests` artifact path; its successful command-only test configuration is documented below:

   ```powershell
   dotnet run --project .\.github\skills\review-pull-request\scripts\PrepareReview.Tests.csproj --artifacts-path "$evidence\helper-tests-artifacts"
   ```

4. **One neutral same-worker capability probe passed.** At SDK/lifecycle validation commit `79fa20de4c51989bbd46eef2023f8c40154c0fa4`, one `general-purpose` / `gpt-5.6-sol` worker was dispatched with `mode: "background"` and no review content or file/tool work. After its completion notification, its actual `LIFECYCLE_INITIAL_OK` result was collected with `read_agent` using `wait: true`. A single `write_agent` follow-up to the same ID succeeded; after the second completion notification, another `read_agent(wait: true, since_turn: 1)` returned `LIFECYCLE_FOLLOWUP_OK; INITIAL=LIFECYCLE_INITIAL_OK`. No replacement worker or retry was used. This proves the exercised runtime capability, not review quality.

5. **One fresh uncoached native review passed at exact SDK/lifecycle validation commit `79fa20de4c51989bbd46eef2023f8c40154c0fa4`.** A new isolated worktree started clean with no `.dotnet` directory and no install-directory overrides. It received only this ordinary top-level request, with no supplied manifest, setup/lifecycle hints, old findings, or subsequent caller intervention:

   > Use review-pull-request to privately review dotnet/aspnetcore#70024 at head d3068c868d2fafeb5f3a37f94c4d8637ce063ed0. Return the completed review here. Do not publish feedback or execute the target PR's product code.

   Actual skill-load events matched the committed body; skill SHA-256 was `2CEFB22E4732D1E66AE857F100A5F6D178813FABDA3C6483B31E13DF06FD3817`, and helper props SHA-256 was `1EA1DA6C30F6F29C4D6F13942E9943375E9940EED1D931136D6BE591D23F08F1`. The reviewer itself ran:

   ```powershell
   . .\activate.ps1; dotnet run .\.github\skills\review-pull-request\scripts\prepare-review.cs -- --pr 70024
   & .\eng\common\dotnet.ps1; if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { exit $LASTEXITCODE }; . .\activate.ps1; dotnet run .\.github\skills\review-pull-request\scripts\prepare-review.cs -- --pr 70024
   ```

   The first command hit the naturally absent SDK; the second installed the pinned SDK12, reactivated, and exited **0** with its own real `ready: true`, version-2 manifest at the exact requested head, merge base `f20cefd359fc632a3c9744a9f79f7514eafe8f2c`, and base tip `ceb0eec49d8d2c77f4f7c26b85ddb6e96940dfed`. The manifest recorded clean guidance commit `79fa20de4c51989bbd46eef2023f8c40154c0fa4`; its SHA-256 was `28C9EAA67F23E364FD1CE34B23A9C0372A7A2A378DDB020E0BB9D4C29A3F59BF`.

   Exactly one prescribed `general-purpose` / `gpt-5.6-sol` worker reviewed the routed cross-cutting guide in background mode; runtime-reported type/model matched. The coordinator collected the actual completed report after notification using `read_agent(wait: true)`, naturally requested clarification from that same worker, and collected its actual completed follow-up after the second notification with `read_agent(wait: true, since_turn: 1)`. No replacement/relaunch occurred. The outer final was **STATUS: NO_FINDINGS**, `PATH: per-guide`, guide **complete**, with one unsupported candidate retained as `UNRESOLVED` rather than accepted. This is completion evidence, not proof of review accuracy. The source worktree remained clean at that exact commit. This historical result is not relabeled as a native review of the later exclusion correction.

6. **Existing model-free checks passed for the SDK/lifecycle change and were refreshed with both the exclusion correction and hosted-read clarification:**

   ```powershell
   .\eng\skill-evals\run.ps1
   $env:PYTHONUTF8='1'; python "$env:USERPROFILE\.copilot\skills\skill-creator\scripts\quick_validate.py" .github\skills\review-pull-request
   git diff --check ceb0eec49d8d2c77f4f7c26b85ddb6e96940dfed HEAD
   ```

   Results: all nine skills linted; four eval schemas validated; both standard and smoke experiments dry-ran with eight plans each (no model or judge execution); quick validation returned `Skill is valid!`; whitespace check passed. The complete diff is limited to the four files above, with 83 insertions and 11 deletions.

### Execution-exclusion regression validation

Follow-up commit: `1bc55952080763403ebbe7afb39be08bb79c5287`. GPT-5.6 Sol and Gemini 4 Argon rubber-ducked the proposed change before implementation and independently checked the final implementation; neither found a blocker.

The actual file-based helper built successfully with the pinned SDK and existing bundled-framework rule, without a target-framework override:

```powershell
dotnet build .\.github\skills\review-pull-request\scripts\prepare-review.cs --artifacts-path "$evidence\exclusion-fileapp-build" --verbosity quiet
```

**Result: exit 0.** The default test command separately remained blocked before assertions:

```powershell
dotnet run --project .\.github\skills\review-pull-request\scripts\PrepareReview.Tests.csproj --artifacts-path "$evidence\exclusion-default-tests"
```

**Result: exit 1, pre-existing MSB3030 missing apphost.** To execute the same helper/test sources on the already installed runtime12 without editing the project or installing another runtime, a validation-only command configuration sets both restore/build target properties and enables apphost generation. An initial `TargetFramework`-only override failed with `NETSDK1005` because restore still selected `net11.0`; setting `TargetFrameworks` as well made restore/build agree:

```powershell
dotnet build .\.github\skills\review-pull-request\scripts\PrepareReview.Tests.csproj -p:TargetFramework=net12.0 -p:UseAppHost=true --artifacts-path "$evidence\exclusion-runtime12-tests" --verbosity quiet
dotnet build .\.github\skills\review-pull-request\scripts\PrepareReview.Tests.csproj -p:TargetFramework=net12.0 -p:TargetFrameworks=net12.0 -p:UseAppHost=true --artifacts-path "$evidence\exclusion-runtime12-tests" --verbosity quiet
```

**Results: first command exit 1 (`NETSDK1005`); second command exit 0, zero warnings/errors.** Subsequent red and green builds used that second command with `--no-restore`; both succeeded with zero warnings/errors. No tracked test-project/framework/configuration changes were made.

With only the regression tests added, before changing the producer/reuse validator, the following focused run failed **all five cases for the expected reasons**: local/remote producer assertions saw the old blanket text; each `scope`, `reason`, and `legacy` reuse row threw no exception. After the fix, the identical selectors passed **5/5**, with no errors, skips, or unrun cases. The first run used `exclusion-red.xml`; the command below records the green run:

```powershell
dotnet "$evidence\exclusion-runtime12-tests\bin\PrepareReview.Tests\debug_net12.0\PrepareReview.Tests.dll" -method PrepareReviewTests.PreparesDistinctCompleteSidesInertTargetInstructionsLargeFilesAndDirtyGuidance -method PrepareReviewTests.SupportsAnImmutableRemoteGuidanceSelection -method PrepareReviewTests.RejectsReuseWithChangedExecutionExclusion -reporter verbose -noColor -xml "$evidence\exclusion-green.xml"
```

**Results: baseline exit 1, 5 failed; candidate exit 0, 5 passed.** Both XML reports were parsed and every theory row's expected red/green outcome checked. These exercise the real preparation and reuse paths against temporary Git fixtures, not target-product code.

The complete existing helper test assembly then ran:

```powershell
dotnet "$evidence\exclusion-runtime12-tests\bin\PrepareReview.Tests\debug_net12.0\PrepareReview.Tests.dll" -reporter quiet -noColor -xml "$evidence\exclusion-full.xml"
```

**Result: exit 0, 64/64 passed, zero errors/failures/skips/unrun cases.** Parsed XML confirmed all 64 actual case results and all three new mutation rows.

### Hosted native-read clarification

Follow-up commit: `a3c072de420dea79caa317c2f661d91299ff9038`. A separate hosted review of #69312, [run 40227035346](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/actions/runs/40227035346), had a successful Actions conclusion but a **BLOCKED source review**, with zero guide workers. Its trusted workflow/guidance revision was `ceb0eec49d8d2c77f4f7c26b85ddb6e96940dfed`, not this PR branch; that result remains blocked.

The exact runtime events distinguish two boundaries. Native whole-file `view` calls for `files.json` (98.0 KB), `pull.json` (34.9 KB), and `feedback.json` (72.0 KB) returned `success: true` but only size warnings, not content. The coordinator then tried three shell `jq` commands. Their permission requests explicitly had `kind: shell`; all completed as `denied-no-approval-rule-and-could-not-request-from-user`, with `Permission denied and could not request permission from user`. No native ranged recovery was attempted for those inputs. The same run had already recovered its oversized manifest through `view_range`, read both complete routed guides, and used native `rg` on the diff.

The workflow intentionally has `bash: false`. The pinned gh-aw v0.92.0 compiler's [tool mapping](https://github.com/github/gh-aw/blob/v0.92.0/pkg/workflow/copilot_engine_tools.go) and [argument construction](https://github.com/github/gh-aw/blob/v0.92.0/pkg/workflow/copilot_engine_execution.go) agree with the recorded Copilot CLI 1.0.80 invocation: `--add-dir /tmp/gh-aw/ --no-ask-user --allow-tool safeoutputs --deny-tool workflow`, without a shell grant. The recorded native `view` schema supports both `view_range` and `forceReadLargeFiles`. This is not evidence of a file ACL, path-length, missing-SDK, or workflow-permission defect. The exact loaded skill instead supplied an incorrect generic recommendation to rerun interactively or with `--allow-all-paths` after that error.

The correction stays in `SKILL.md`: hosted coordinators/workers must use already-authorized native readers/searches, page large inputs, and not treat size warnings as content. A shell-execution denial calls for reading the same frozen input natively, not a rerun or broader permissions; explicit file-access/content-exclusion denials must never be worked around, and genuinely unavailable required bytes still yield `BLOCKED`. The supported force-read option is limited to an oversized single line and complete returned content. Hosted worker briefs explicitly carry the native-only/paging/no-shell rules. No workflow, shell grant, target execution, publication capability, worker configuration, or evidence gate changes.

GPT-5.6 Sol and Gemini 4 Argon approved the bounded proposal before implementation. The model-free checks above passed again. A read-only local mechanism check used native `view` with `view_range` on representative slices of all three oversized JSON inputs in a retained local #69312 bundle: `[1,14]`, `[1,20]`, and `[1,22]`, respectively. All returned actual bounded content without warnings or truncation. The local `files.json` hash is identical to the hosted input; local pull/feedback are different captures, not claimed as the exact hosted inputs.

**This is not a corrected hosted-run result.** No upstream `/review` repost, workflow run, or duplicate fork integration was performed. The separately owned staged fork diagnostic must establish actual required source reads, returned prescribed workers covering every routed guide, and final synthesis; green Actions alone is insufficient. Existing #69312 local S/O/G evidence stays pinned at `1bc55952...`; a new local skill does not change the still-default-branch upstream hosted lane.

**Limits:** helper tests above ran only in the disclosed command-only .NET 12 configuration; the default explicit .NET 11 test configuration is still blocked and is not claimed to pass. The full native-review result remains evidence at `79fa20de...`, not at either follow-up commit; no new native review or optional target repro was run for these follow-ups. Local native JSON slices establish only the illustrated reader mechanism, not complete hosted source/guide coverage or unaided compliance with the new wording. The observed Windows setup/bootstrap and helper contract do not establish non-Windows execution, target-product behavior, review accuracy, or controlled wording-only model uplift. No target PR product code was executed or review feedback published.
